title: Regional load-drain circuit-breaker + escalation play for cross-region degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Over the last six weeks we observed three separate customer escalations where a subset of hosted and dedicated customers experienced 30-80% increased token latency and elevated error rates for 10-90 minutes during regional traffic bursts. Symptoms point to asymmetric routing and backend queue amplification when one region's control plane briefly lags (control-plane API timeouts, KV cache thrash). Impact: customer-facing latency spikes, increased 5xxs, and some customers on Dedicated reported SLA violations. Goal: ship a tested operational playbook + an automated regional 'load-drain' circuit-breaker that temporarily rebalances traffic away from affected region(s) when key signals cross thresholds, plus a hotfix to routing policy to stop aggressive sticky routing during transient control-plane errors.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook documented and validated in playbook tests (synthetic chaos) for both Hosted and Dedicated deployments
Circuit-breaker implemented: threshold-based detection + automated traffic rebalancing to fallback region or dedicated spare pool
Telemetry: dashboard shows region-level incoming RPS, queue depth, average token latency, 5xx rate; alerting thresholds in PagerDuty configured
Canary rollout: feature enabled in a single low-risk region for 48h with automated health checks, then progressive rollout to remaining regions
Customer-facing mitigation template and postmortem checklist ready in Drive and support playbooks linked
comments: 2026-03-05 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage summary and escalation sequence attached. Hypothesis: routing control-plane timeouts + KV cache misses causing amplified backpressure. Linking incident timelines.

2026-03-06 - Rohit Singh: Spike reproduced in staging by throttling control-plane API and introducing 200ms egress jitter; observed queue buildup in runtime shards. Started design doc for circuit-breaker logic.
2026-03-08 - Priya Desai (SRE): Reviewed detection signals. Suggested adding 'prefix-KV-miss-rate' and 'runtime-kv-resync-duration' as inputs so we don't misfire on normal scale events.

2026-03-09 - Rohit Singh: Implemented prototype circuit-breaker in routing-proxy with two modes: DRY_RUN and ENFORCE. DRY_RUN will emit events to '#ops-circuit-debug' and won't change traffic. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proxy/pull/2197
2026-03-10 - Support (Maya Torres): Drafted customer communication templates and a transient-SLA-acknowledgement procedure for Dedicated customers impacted during rollouts.

2026-03-11 - Engineering Lead (Ethan Park): Approved experiment to enable DRY_RUN for us-east-2 for 48h; requirement: no customer-visible increase in error rate and no more than 5% additional latency deviation.

2026-03-12 - Rohit Singh: Canary started in us-east-2 with DRY_RUN. Initial metrics look promising: detection fired twice for subslice and routing decisions logged. Next step: small ENFORCE rollout to non-production tenants for 6h.
Planned follow-ups: post-canonicalization of thresholds, add a safety net to ensure dedicated customers with pinned-capacity are excluded from automated rebalancing unless explicitly opted-in.
